blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team wants a linter to run after every file edit, with no reliance on Claude remembering. Which feature fits, and why?

options.text: A skill, because Claude reads it before each change
options.says: Ruled out because with a skill, "Claude interprets the instructions; outcome can vary."

options.text: A hook, because it fires on its event and the trigger is guaranteed
options.says: The page says a hook "Always fires on its event; the trigger is guaranteed".

options.text: A line in the project file, because it is read at the start of a session
options.says: Ruled out because an instruction in the project file "is a request, not a guarantee".

options.text: An output style, because it applies to the whole session
options.says: Ruled out because "Claude follows both as instructions, so neither is enforced."

questions.stem: A team uses the same set of skills, hooks and MCP servers in six repositories. What does the documentation suggest?

options.text: Package them as one plugin that each repository installs
options.says: The page says "A plugin bundles skills, hooks, subagents, and MCP servers into a single installable unit", for "the same setup in several repositories, or to share it".

options.text: Copy the files into each repository by hand and keep them in step
options.says: Ruled out because the trigger is "A second repository needs the same setup", which calls for a plugin.

options.text: Put the whole set into one long CLAUDE.md in each repository
options.says: Ruled out because CLAUDE.md is paid for on "every request", and the guidance is "Keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines."

options.text: Convert every item into a subagent that is spawned for each task
options.says: Ruled out because a subagent is "an isolated worker with its own context", not a packaging unit.

questions.stem: A workflow that deploys to production must never start unless a person types its name. Which setting does the page give?

options.text: `disable-model-invocation: true`, which hides it until you invoke it yourself
options.says: The page says to use `disable-model-invocation: true`: "This saves context and ensures only you trigger them."

options.text: A longer description, which makes Claude hesitate before it considers using it
options.says: Ruled out because "If descriptions are vague or overlap, Claude may load the wrong skill or miss one that would help", which is no control.

options.text: A line in CLAUDE.md that asks Claude to wait for a person to approve the run
options.says: Ruled out because a line in CLAUDE.md "is a request, not a guarantee".

options.text: An output style that makes every reply shorter and more formal for the user
options.says: Ruled out because an output style sets "a voice, length or format wanted in every response", and says nothing about starting skills.

origin.section: What each one costs in context

questions.stem: A project has an API style guide of 3,000 lines that matters only when endpoints are written. Where does it belong?

options.text: In CLAUDE.md, so that it is available in every session
options.says: Ruled out because "CLAUDE.md is paid for on every request", and "Keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines."

options.text: In an output style, so that it shapes each response
options.says: Ruled out because an output style is "a voice, length or format wanted in every response", not a library of facts.

options.text: In a skill, which loads the full content only when used
options.says: The page says reference material goes to skills, "which load on demand", while "descriptions at start, full content when used" keeps the cost low.

options.text: In an MCP server, so that Claude can open it as a connection
options.says: Ruled out because MCP "connects Claude to external services", and a local guide is knowledge, not a service: "MCP for knowledge."

origin.section: What each one costs in context

questions.stem: A platform team wants a note posted to the team chat whenever any Claude Code session closes, in forty repositories. What fits?

options.text: A chat server for the service, delivered through one plugin
options.says: Ruled out because "an MCP server only offers tools that Claude may or may not call; nothing fires at the end".

options.text: A script fired by the end-of-work event, delivered through one plugin
options.says: Row 12 gives a hook for "Post a message to the team channel when a session ends". A plugin is how the same hook reaches many repositories: "A plugin bundles skills, hooks, subagents, and MCP servers into a single installable unit".

options.text: A skill with the posting steps, delivered through one plugin
options.says: Ruled out because "Anything written in text, CLAUDE.md, a skill or an output style, is followed as an instruction", and an instruction is not an event.

options.text: A line in each instruction file, copied into every project
options.says: Ruled out because "a line in the instruction file is a request, not a guarantee".
